description: Synthetic defect-seeding test set for Bifrost governance node (S2-2, Wave 6, Agent E deliverable). All data is fabricated for testing purposes and does not represent real Goertek business data.

test_cases.description: Critical production fields (quantity, product_id, revenue_cny, yield_rate, line_code) contain NULL values across 24 of 60 rows.
PLANT-03 records unit_price_cny in 万元 scale while other plants use 元 scale in the same column, producing a bimodal distribution with a 10000x gap.
Composite key (date, line_code, sku_id) has 8 duplicate rows forming 4 duplicate pairs with identical field values, indicating ETL duplicate extraction.
yield_rate and utilization_rate columns (semantic: ratio, domain [0,1]) contain 7 impossible values including negative ratios and ratios exceeding 1.0.
Daily production time series is missing 3 scattered working days (2026-02-04, 2026-02-05, 2026-02-18) after correctly excluding weekends and a known planned-maintenance window.
line_code column contains 8 rows (10%) referencing 3 production-line codes not present in the dimension table, concentrated in the most recent records.
Statistically extreme 8-10x sales spike over 3 days that is a legitimate promotional event (promo_tag='promo_6_1_mid_year'), not a data defect. Tests governance's false-positive filtering.

metadata.author: Agent E (S2-2 Wave 6)
red_lines: Synthetic Data Labeling: All fixtures are synthetic. Mark them as such in manifest metadata and CSV headers. Never fabricate real Goertek business data.
No Placeholders: Every CSV must be parseable and contain realistic column names/values. No "TODO", "PLACEHOLDER", or stub content.
Ground Truth Accuracy: expected.json must precisely describe what defect was seeded and where. This is the test oracle.
DefectType Enum Coverage: Cover all 6 core enum values from packages/contracts/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/Defect/properties/defect_type plus at least one false-anomaly case.
metadata.row_index_convention: 0-based over data rows (header excluded). Verified against 01/02/04, whose expected.json affected_rows match 0-based positions exactly.

revisions.rationale: Four input.csv files did not actually contain the defect their expected.json asserts, so they could not serve as a governance-accuracy oracle. Per fixtures red line 'Ground Truth Accuracy: expected.json ... is the test oracle', every expected.json was left byte-for-byte unchanged and the input data was corrected to match it. No oracle was weakened to fit the data.

changes.problem: The 4 declared duplicate pairs shared only the date column, so the composite key (date, line_code, sku_id) produced 0 duplicate groups and expected.json's 'identical field values across all columns' was false.
changes.fix: For each pair in evidence.duplicate_pairs, copied row a over row b in full.
changes.verified: 4 duplicate groups at rows [15,16,38,39,62,63,89,90] == affected_rows; duplicate_count 8; total_rows 120; ratio 6.7%; every pair identical across all columns.

changes.problem: The generator cycled input_qty over {1000..1700 step 50} and output_qty over {950..1390 step 40} at different phases, so output_qty overtook input_qty in blocks. 28 rows carried derived yield_rate > 1 on top of the 5 seeded ones, making the declared 5%/7-row violation count false.
changes.fix: For each overshoot row, lowered output_qty to the largest value on the generator's own lattice (950+40k) below input_qty, and recomputed yield_rate = round(output_qty/input_qty, 4). The 5 seeded yield_rate cells and 2 seeded utilization_rate cells were left byte-identical (row 45 keeps its injected 1.08 despite its output_qty changing).
changes.verified: yield violations exactly [12,27,45,68,83] with values [1.12,-0.03,1.08,1.15,-0.01]; utilization violations [34,71] with [1.23,-0.05]; merged affected_rows [12,27,34,45,68,71,83]; 0 rows with output_qty > input_qty remain; all 95 non-seeded rows satisfy yield_rate == round(output_qty/input_qty, 4) and lie in [0,1].

changes.problem: Dates ran 2026-01-04..2026-03-30, one day earlier than the declared range, and the absent working days did not line up with the declared gaps.
changes.fix: Shifted the whole date column +1 day to restore the declared range, then moved the three present-but-should-be-absent dates (2026-02-04, 2026-02-18, 2026-03-09) onto the three absent-but-should-be-present dates (2026-02-06, 2026-02-19, 2026-03-11) and re-sorted. daily_output_qty values were not touched.
changes.verified: range 2026-01-05..2026-03-31; calendar_days 86; expected_working_days 62; actual_data_days 57; weekends_excluded 24; missing_working_days exactly [2026-02-04,2026-02-05,2026-02-18]; planned_downtime_excluded exactly [2026-03-09,2026-03-10]; gap_count 3; gap_ratio 4.8%; 0 weekend rows; no duplicate dates.

changes.problem: expected.json declares planned_downtime_excluded [2026-03-09, 2026-03-10], but nothing in the directory declared that window. d03-temporal-gap makes the business calendar a premise of the judgement, so a detector reading only input.csv necessarily finds 5 missing working days instead of the declared 3.
changes.fix: Added calendar.json declaring the planned-downtime window as data, alongside time_grain and the same SYNTHETIC_GOERTEK_FIXTURE data_label. The window is now a project input rather than an assumption compiled into the detector.
changes.verified: With calendar.json present the detector reports exactly the 3 declared missing_working_days; deleting it returns the count to 5. test_05_planned_downtime_comes_from_the_calendar_file deletes the file and asserts that regression, so an implementation that hardcodes those two dates fails.

changes.problem: The case declared a dimension table but the directory contained only input.csv, so the referential check had nothing to join against.
changes.fix: Added dimension-line.csv holding exactly the 4 valid_codes from expected.json (LINE-F01..F04), carrying the same SYNTHETIC_GOERTEK_FIXTURE data_label as every other fixture file.
changes.verified: valid_codes and dangling_codes [LINE-NEW-05,06,07] match; dangling rows [72..79] == affected_rows; dangling_row_count 8; total_rows 80; ratio 10%; case- and whitespace-normalized intersection of dangling and valid codes is empty, so the break is genuinely referential and not a formatting artifact.

unchanged: All seven expected.json files (byte-identical to v1.0).

01-missing-value/input.csv, 02-unit-inconsistent/input.csv, 07-false-anomaly-promo-spike/input.csv — re-verified against their oracles and already correct. 07 in particular: promo rows at [31,32,33] with max/p50 = 8.9x, which must stay below d01's 100x bimodal threshold so the false-positive filter is actually exercised.
